I'd like to expand this request into a broader alignment of `gemini.txt` with other instructions, especially since it hasn't been updated in 10 months.

I would propose adding at least:
- instructions to use `todowrite` more effectively
- a no-emoji clause 🥲 Gemini models are the only ones I've observed thus far (I have tested across Kimi, Qwen, GPT/Codex, DeepSeek, GLM, and a few other models) consistently use emojis

> An alternate approach we could do is for Desktop to download and install the CLI as it's running, defaulting to the installation script curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash or using bun/brew/etc if an older version is already installed.

At least for my use case, this would fail - silently or otherwise - due to firewall rules in place.

Having a deb and rpm for the cli, for offline and intentional installation would be great.

On that front, @simonklee mentioned:

> Disable self-upgrade

Taking the deb/rpm option "to the next level" would be having deb and rpm repositories and allow the package managers to discover when updates are available, though understandably that would greatly increase the scope of things.

Same here. Behavior: 
Recently I upgraded from [v1.14.41](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/tree/v1.14.41) to version [v1.14.48](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/tree/v1.14.48):

```
⚙ Read [file_path=/tmp/[REDACTED].json]
Model tried to call unavailable tool 'invalid'. Available tools: .
Thinking: The Read tool seems to be unavailable. Let me try using bash to read the file instead, but the instructions say to use Read tool. Let me check if there's a different tool name or try another approach. Actually, looking at the available tools list, it seems empty. Let me try bash cat first to see if I can read the file, then proceed.

⚙ Bash [command=cat /tmp/[REDACTED].json, description=Read round payload file]
Model tried to call unavailable tool 'invalid'. Available tools: .
Thinking: The tools seem unavailable. Let me try with a different approach - maybe I need to just provide the JSON inline since I can't read the file. Wait, the instructions say I MUST read the payload file. Let me check if there's something wrong with my tool usage. Looking at the tool spec, it seems I should use:
functions.Read:2<|tool_call_argument_begin|>{"file_path": "/tmp/[REDACTED].json"}
But it returned "unavailable tool 'invalid'". Let me try bash differently.
...
```

model was kimi k2.6. After revert to v1.14.41 everything started to work again.

It took a while to track down why my config started breaking, but this is it. This change effectively breaks the ability to pass a custom compaction prompt in configs. It introduces an opinionated, hard-coded compaction process that LLMs will follow in favor of anything written in the config. I can no longer compact to a format I specify to get additional details about the previous session context, the sub-agents it ran within, their session IDs, their summary documents, and it is breaking my long-running workflows. This needs to be reverted, just integrated into the default compaction prompt, or some escape hatch to disable this needs to be introduced that isn't me creating a custom plugin to wipe out this behavior.

What was this trying to solve @nexxeln? There's no background info on this change that I can see or linking issue that this fixes.

I’d split the fix into two layers: per-call retry policy at the tool boundary, and attempt-level admission at the loop boundary.

The first stops identical edit/write failures from hammering the same tool forever. The second decides whether the next attempt should run at all after N same-class failures. The important part is to emit a first-class stop reason, not just "gave up," so users can tell schema failure from budget failure from verifier failure. We ended up caring a lot about that distinction in MartinLoop because the expensive bug is usually not the single tool failure, it’s the ungoverned attempt that keeps going after the failure is already obvious.

For keybind-related issues, please also check our pinned keybinds documentation: #4997

I can reproduce a related Fedora/RPM update/version mismatch on Fedora with the latest desktop RPM.

Manual install command used:

```sh
sudo dnf install ./opencode-desktop-linux-x86_64.rpm
```

DNF/RPM reports the package was upgraded successfully:

```text
opencode-1.14.48-1.x86_64
```

But the installed CLI sidecar still reports an older version:

```sh
/usr/bin/opencode-cli --version
# 1.14.33
```

The desktop launcher/alternative appears to point to the newly installed app correctly:

```text
readlink -f /usr/bin/@opencode-aidesktop
/opt/OpenCode/@opencode-aidesktop

update-alternatives --display @opencode-aidesktop
@opencode-aidesktop - status is auto.
 link currently points to /opt/OpenCode/@opencode-aidesktop
/opt/OpenCode/@opencode-aidesktop - priority 100
Current `best' version is /opt/OpenCode/@opencode-aidesktop.
```

The UI still shows OpenCode Desktop v1.14.33 and keeps showing an update notification for v1.14.48, even after manually installing the v1.14.48 RPM.

So this may not only be the in-app updater failing. The v1.14.48 RPM seems to install as v1.14.48 at the package level, but still includes or uses an older `opencode-cli`/sidecar version (1.14.33), which may be what the UI is displaying/checking against.

Install transaction also printed this scriptlet warning:

```text
/usr/bin/@opencode-aidesktop has not been configured as an alternative for @opencode-aidesktop
```

Environment:
- Fedora/RPM install via DNF
- Package: `opencode-1.14.48-1.x86_64`
- Desktop RPM asset: `opencode-desktop-linux-x86_64.rpm`
- Installed CLI sidecar reports: `1.14.33`

## Can we delete `src/util/filesystem.ts` entirely?

### 1. Current shape of `src/util/filesystem.ts`

245 lines. Exports by category:

**Pure (sync, no IO) — already duplicated on `AppFileSystem`:**
`normalizePath` (filesystem.ts:113), `normalizePathPattern` (:123), `resolve` (:135), `windowsPath` (:145), `overlaps` (:158), `contains` (:164).

**Sync wrapper around `node:fs`:** `stat` (:22) — returns `Stats | undefined` via `statSync(p, {throwIfNoEntry: false})`. 6 callers; NOT on AppFileSystem.

**Async wrappers around `fs/promises`/`existsSync` — the actual targets:**
- `exists` (:10) → `AppFileSystem.existsSafe` (70 callers)
- `isDir` (:14) → `AppFileSystem.isDir` (4 callers)
- `statAsync` (:26) — **NOT on AppFileSystem** (6 callers)
- `size` (:33) — **NOT on AppFileSystem** (3 callers)
- `readText` (:38) → `fs.readFileString` (40 callers)
- `readJson` (:42) → `AppFileSystem.readJson` (25 callers)
- `readBytes` (:46) — **NOT on AppFileSystem** (3 callers)
- `readArrayBuffer` (:50) — **NOT on AppFileSystem** (2 callers)
